subject: mathematics
title: Fraction Models Review
objective: Represent fractions equal to one or greater than one using equal parts.
introduction: Milo shades equal star spaces on a chart. Can you tell when the shaded fraction fills one whole or covers more?

vocabulary.definition: Three thirds fill one whole, so three thirds equal one.
Four thirds has a bigger numerator, so it is more than one whole.
A fraction counts parts that are all the same size.

activities.instruction: Watch equal parts show one whole or more than one.
activities.content: A fraction model must have equal-sized parts. If shaded parts equal all parts, it is one whole; if shaded parts are more, it is greater than one.

feedback.retry: Check that all parts are the same size before comparing counts.

items.explanation: 3/3 equals 1 because the numerator and denominator are the same: three thirds fill one whole. 3/4 and 2/3 are less than one, and 4/3 is greater than one whole.

items.prompt: Which fraction is greater than one?
items.explanation: 4/3 is greater than 1 because the numerator 4 is bigger than the denominator 3, so the fraction is greater than one whole. 3/5 and 1/4 are less than one, and 2/2 equals one.

items.prompt: Milo cuts a cake into 4 pieces to show 3/4. What must be true?

options.text: all 4 pieces are the same size
one piece is smaller than the rest
the cake is cut into 3 pieces

items.explanation: 3/4 names 3 of 4 equal parts, so all 4 pieces must be the same size. If the pieces are different sizes, they are not equal parts.

items.prompt: A shape has 5 equal parts and all 5 parts are shaded. Which fraction does it show?
items.explanation: All 5 equal parts are shaded, so the fraction is 5/5, and 5/5 = 1 whole. 1/5 and 4/5 shade only part of the shape, and 5/6 needs 6 parts.

items.prompt: A circle is split into 3 equal parts and all 3 are shaded. Which fraction is shown?
items.explanation: The circle has 3 equal parts and all 3 are shaded, so the fraction is 3/3, which equals one whole. 3/4, 2/3, and 4/5 need different numbers of parts.
